title: Cross-SDK failover, jitter/backoff defaults, and idempotency usage examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
We need a single, opinionated set of retry and failover defaults that are safe for production across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, plus clear guidance and language examples for idempotency keys and streaming resume behavior. Existing docs scattered across PRs and internal notes have produced inconsistent client behavior (duplicate operations, long client-side hangs, and confusing TLDRs on when clients should retry).

Goal:
- Define conservative but practical defaults for exponential backoff + jitter and failover ordering (region -> model-variant -> degrade-to-smaller-model).
- Provide idempotency key semantics: recommended header, lifetime, client vs SDK generation, and server-side enforcement expectations.
- Define a retryable error taxonomy tailored to Redwood Inference semantics (auth, transient infra, model overload, user errors, streaming truncation/resume).
- Ship examples for Python/TS/Go and a short cookbook demonstrating safe streaming resume and idempotency patterns.

Proposed defaults (opinionated):
- Initial backoff (base): 100ms
- Multiplier: 2.0
- Max backoff: 10s
- Max attempts: 5 (configurable per call)
- Jitter strategy: full jitter (random between base and current backoff) to avoid thundering herd
- Failover order when a request is marked retryable: 1) local region variant, 2) matched alternative model family (smaller quantized variant), 3) cross-region fallback (if customer config allows), 4) degraded-mode with partial responses (if enabled)

Idempotency guidance:
- Header name: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (string UUID recommended)
- SDK behavior: prefer client-provided key; if omitted, SDK SHOULD NOT auto-generate for non-idempotent user ops (e.g., create-charge). For simple generation flows (batch inference where dedup is desired), SDK MAY generate a key when the client opts in via options.idempotency = true.
- TTL: server-side TTL for idempotency dedup: 24 hours by default for hosted; configurable per-customer in Dedicated/Private. SDKs should expose cache hints (Warning: previous-response-cached) when responses were deduplicated.
- Duplication semantics: server returns 409 with X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status when a duplicate is rejected, and returns 200 with X-Redwood-Idempotency-Status: replay when it replayed a previous response.

Streaming-specific rules:
- For resumable streams, server emits resume cursor tokens periodically in-stream under structured output metadata (cursor ids). If a streaming connection is lost: 1) client SHOULD retry only from the last confirmed token; 2) retries must carry the same idempotency key when the operation is logically identical; 3) SDKs MUST expose an ergonomic helper that resumes automatically when cursor tokens are present.
- If model-side work is incremental and cannot be resumed, server marks stream as non-resumable; client SDKs should surface that flag and avoid generating automatic retries.

Retryable error taxonomy (high-level):
- Retryable transient infra (safe): 429 (rate limit with Retry-After <= 10s), 503, 502, 504, network timeouts, transient TLS handshake failures.
- Retryable with backoff but careful (conditional): 429 with long Retry-After (>10s) -> surface to customer; auth-expiry (401) -> do not retry unless credentials refreshed automatically by SDK.
- Non-retryable (client/user): 400, 401 (invalid creds), 403, 422 (validation), semantic model errors.
- Streaming-specific: connection aborted mid-stream -> treat as conditional retryable only if server provided resume cursor recently; otherwise non-retryable and surface partial output.

Telemetry and observability expectations:
- Counters: sdk.retry.attempts, sdk.retry.successes, sdk.idempotency.duplicates, sdk.stream.resumes, sdk.failover.events
- Tagging: model, region, route, idempotency_key_present (true/false)

Language ergonomics and examples (summary):
- Python: high-level helper RetryPolicy dataclass, and stream.resume_from(cursor) utility. Example shows using context manager with auto-retries but explicit opt-in for idempotency generation.
- TypeScript: fluent builder pattern for RetryOptions + built-in fetch wrapper that injects jitter. Example demonstrates automatic abort signal wiring and explicit idempotency header setting.
- Go: functional options on Client with RetryPolicy and ResumeStream(ctx, cursor) helper; example shows how to generate UUID v4 idempotency keys and attach them to requests.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- TTL length: shorter TTL reduces accidental dedup but increases risk of duplicated downstream operations. We chose 24h default as conservative for inference workloads, but enterprise customers can limit.
- Should SDKs auto-generate idempotency keys? We prefer opt-in to avoid accidental dedup of distinct logical operations.
- Failover ordering: prioritizing local-region lower-latency failovers reduces cross-region egress costs and preserves data locality but may worsen availability in regional incidents; allow customer override.

Acceptance criteria:
- Draft spec merged in RFC: docs.redwood.internal/sdk-retry-failover-spec (link below).
- SDK PRs in python-sdk, ts-sdk, go-sdk implementing defaults + examples.
- Unit tests covering idempotency header behavior and stream resume helper.
- Telemetry events emitted when retries/failovers occur and a dashboard tile in Console for the next release.

Attachments and references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/SDK/Retry+and+Failover+RFC
- Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/412; https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/88; https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/207
